concepts.def: A small unit that data is split into for transmission, made of a header, payload and trailer.
Splitting data into packets that travel independently across a network and are reassembled in order at the destination.
Sending data one bit at a time down a single wire — slower but reliable over long distances.
Sending several bits at once down multiple wires — fast but only reliable over short distances.
Data transmission in one direction only, e.g. from a keyboard to a computer.
Data can travel both ways but only one direction at a time, e.g. a walkie-talkie.
Data travels in both directions at the same time, e.g. a phone call.
Error detection using a parity bit to keep the number of 1s odd or even.
Error detection where a calculated value is sent with the data and recalculated at the destination to check it matches.
Error detection where received data is sent back to the sender and compared with the original.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Transmission — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Transmission brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Transmission.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: The first one added (FIFO).
Variables that change type at runtime.

It can explode or be damaged easily.
It can store data permanently.
Variables that change type at runtime.
Having multiple classes with the same name.
Variables that change type at runtime.

Any item, randomly.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Casting”?
options: Ordered sequence of characters, used to store text such as names or sentences.
Whole number with no fractional part, positive, negative or zero (e.g., 7, -42, 0).
Number with a fractional part stored using floating-point representation (e.g., 3.14).
Converting a value from one data type to another, e.g., int("5") gives integer 5.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Real / float”?
options: Data type with only two possible values: True or False, used for logical conditions.
Whole number with no fractional part, positive, negative or zero (e.g., 7, -42, 0).
Number with a fractional part stored using floating-point representation (e.g., 3.14).
Single letter, digit or symbol, typically stored using ASCII or Unicode codes.
